name: Hermes Agent
prerequisites: hermes >=0.19.0 installed and on PATH (git install, pipx, or the install script); the CLI is a Python console script, so the binary is a shim into <HERMES_HOME>/hermes-agent/venv/bin/hermes
an inference provider configured in <HERMES_HOME>/config.yaml (model.default + model.provider) with credentials in <HERMES_HOME>/.env or auth.json — e.g. 'hermes setup' or 'hermes login'
HERMES_HOME exported to the recording home, so the run writes to an isolated state.db instead of the maintainer's real session store
the sqlite3 CLI on PATH — hermes persists no transcript file, so the driver reads session id and turn-completion straight out of state.db

LIVE TOOL ROSTER (probed 2026-08-03 against hermes 0.19.0 on this machine, 36 callable functions): read_file, write_file, patch, search_files, terminal and web_search are ALL ABSENT — do NOT write a recipe that assumes them. execute_code exists but is Docker-backed and fails here ("docker version" failed). skills_list and skill_view are verified-working tool calls and are the ones to reach for when a cell needs a real tool call. Three recordings were burned rediscovering this; re-probe the roster before trusting it against a different HERMES_HOME or a newer CLI.

TIMING: prefer WIDE generations (e.g. a 30-line count plus two sentences of prose). The store watcher polls every 2s with a 500ms debounce, so a ~1s turn can commit its inbound user row and its assistant finish_reason='stop' row inside a SINGLE scan — the ready→working edge then never exists and any tN_start phase fails. Observed margins on the 2026-08-03 sweep: widened turns gave 1.7s–5.4s working spans, i.e. barely more than one scan gap at the low end. Widen the generation; never weaken the spec.

ROOT CAUSE of the missing tools (traced 2026-08-03, supersedes the flat 'they are ABSENT' reading of the roster note above): the terminal AND file toolsets are not missing from hermes, they are GATED OFF by the recording home's config.yaml, which sets `terminal.backend: docker` while this machine's Docker daemon is down. tools/terminal_tool.py::check_terminal_requirements() shells out to `docker version` for the docker backend (exit 1 here: 'Cannot connect to the Docker daemon at unix:///Users/ingo/.docker/run/docker.sock'), and tools/__init__.py::check_file_requirements gates read_file/write_file/patch/search_files the same way — the loader prints 'check_fn check_terminal_requirements returned False' and 'check_fn _check_file_reqs returned False' at startup. Setting `terminal.backend: local` makes check_terminal_requirements return True immediately and restores write_file/patch/terminal (and with them the check_all_command_guards classifier that 2.11 auto-classified-permission needs). That is a MAINTAINER decision, not a recorder's: it hands the live agent host shell access on this machine, which is presumably why the docker backend was configured in the first place. Until it is taken, keep writing recipes against the callable roster.
